html:
This is the Yukon part of the land of the Teslin Tlingit, around Teslin Lake in the southern Yukon. The council's lands also reach into British Columbia; see Teslin Tlingit Council (BC).

The Teslin Tlingit are Inland Tlingit, whose ancestors came inland from the coast around the Taku River to trade and then settled by the lake. They kept the coastal clan system, with Wolf and Crow halves. They lived by hunting, trapping and fishing, and traded furs with the coast.

The Alaska Highway, built in 1942, ran right through the village of Teslin and changed life there quickly. In 1993 the Teslin Tlingit Council signed one of the first Yukon land claim and self-government agreements, and it runs its own justice system based on its clans. Their neighbours include the Carcross/Tagish.
